clue.text: Bog paper defines shareholders' meeting

indicators.note: to define is to mark the bounds of something, so the paper's letters form a border round the meeting

parts.note: a quire is a set of sheets of paper, traditionally 24 or 25
AGM is the annual general meeting of a company's shareholders

explanation.surface: A newspaper explains what goes on at a company's annual meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog paper' looks like a single phrase about lavatory paper, but the clue splits after 'Bog'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog is soft, wet, sinking ground, which is exactly what a quagmire is.

clue.text: Minute can start to yawn

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first of yawn is used

explanation.surface: A short tin of something might make you yawn from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, is an adjective meaning extremely small.

clue.text: Spot the woman's instrument

parts.note: a zit is slang for a spot or pimple
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A pimple-spotting remark about some woman's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a stringed instrument plucked as it lies flat.

clue.text: Relative takes a bit of tweed for top of pillbox hat

indicators.note: the relative takes in a new letter, one half of a swap signal
one letter stands in for another, completing the swap signal

parts.note: a stepson is a relative by marriage

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here of pillbox
just a small bit, the first letter, of tweed is used

explanation.surface: A family member swaps a pillbox hat for something in tweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... for' signals a substitution: the P of STEPSON (top of pillbox) is replaced by T (a bit of tweed).
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the wide-brimmed cowboy hat named after its maker.

clue.text: Greek character's back to front in photo — sorry!

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photo

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the Greek letter name is moved round to its front

parts.note: theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An apology for a Greek person photographed facing the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' here means the back letter goes to the front, not a full reversal; 'sorry!' passes for an apology but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry used as an adjective, as in a sorry state, means feeble or pitiful.

clue.text: Dad staged riot — it's old fashioned masculine, national pride

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: something staged is set up or arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: 'tis is an archaic contraction of it is
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: Father organised a riot, and it's the old-fashioned macho kind of national fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staged' rearranges RIOT to TRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotism is love of and devotion to one's country.

clue.text: Is able to rise in low country

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: to low is to moo, as a cow does

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: Something about getting up in the Low Countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' signals reading upwards in this down clue. 'low country' suggests the Netherlands, but low is what a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny independent principality on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Boxer dog I advertise for sale

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
to list something is to put it up for sale

explanation.surface: An ad: a boxer dog for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer dog' reads as the breed, but Boxer is the definition and the dog is a pug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a fighter with fists, a prizefighter.

clue.text: Edges of aluminium razor shaved face of noble warrior

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, here of aluminium
a word shaved has its ends trimmed off, leaving the middle of razor
the face of a word is its front letter

explanation.surface: A noble warrior's face shaved with an aluminium razor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a legendary race of female warriors in Greek myth.

clue.text: Snug Lycra's unattractive

indicators.note: read as 'has', the phrase holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Tight-fitting stretchy sportswear is not a good look.
explanation.walkthrough: The only signal is the 's, read as 'has': Snug Lycra has the answer within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Had consumed one dry sandwich to get going

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the others, as if eating them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
TT means teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking
a hero is an American long submarine sandwich

explanation.surface: Someone ate a single dry sandwich before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwich' looks like the containment signal, but it is the HERO, a long American sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the road is an idiom for setting off on a journey or leaving.

clue.text: Captain missing first bit of smoked fish

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for captain goes missing

parts.note: a skipper is a ship's or team captain

explanation.surface: A captain without his first course of smoked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a herring that has been split, salted and smoked.

clue.text: Dancing polka will lead to terribly intimate conversation

indicators.note: letters that dance are moved about, so they are rearranged
the lead of a word is its first letter, here of terribly

explanation.surface: Dancing the polka will lead to some terribly intimate chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillow talk is the private chat of lovers in bed.

clue.text: Steer without crashing hot-rod, as is customary

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the steer goes around the rest

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

indicators.note: a crashing car is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A driving tip: steer clear of crashing your hot-rod, as is usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense, outside, so the steer goes around the anagram that 'crashing' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means conventional, following accepted practice.

clue.text: Cockney crook cooked a fat eel

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked up or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An East End villain prepared a plump eel, a Cockney delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, a tea leaf is a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea leaf rhymes with thief, so in London slang it names a criminal.

clue.text: Heard an Acting Chancellor had a large snake

indicators.note: heard means the words are listened to, so they are sounded

parts.note: taken as written; Anna Chancellor is a British actress, so an acting Chancellor is Anna; to be had is to be fooled, so had means conned; taken as written

explanation.surface: Rumour says a stand-in finance minister owned a big snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna Chancellor is an English actress (Four Weddings and a Funeral); 'had' means fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American constrictor of the boa family.

clue.text: Specs, oddly found outside home for writers

indicators.note: these letters are found around the other piece
the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of specs

parts.note: a crib is slang for a home or pad

explanation.surface: Glasses, curiously, found outside the house for some writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribes are people who copied out documents by hand, so writers.

clue.text: Outfit's three points on detailed logo

parts.note: E, N and S are three compass points

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail, the final letter, removed

parts.note: an emblem is a logo or badge

explanation.surface: A clothing outfit's logo with three points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed: EMBLEM loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a set of clothes worn together, or a musical group.

clue.text: Rebuild the timeless Clive Sinclair C5, for example

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the parts together in a new arrangement
time is T in physics, so timeless means the letter T is removed from the word the

explanation.surface: Restore Clive Sinclair's ageless C5 electric trike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T from THE, leaving HE, which 'Rebuild' shuffles with CLIVE. The Sinclair C5 was a notorious 1985 British electric tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinclair C5 was a small battery-powered tricycle, an example of a road conveyance.

clue.text: Spoil backing of legato bassoon piece

indicators.note: going backwards, the letters are read in reverse
a piece of the phrase, so the answer is taken from within it

explanation.surface: Ruin the backing track of a smooth bassoon solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' takes EGATOBAS from legato bassoon, and 'backing' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage as a verb means deliberately to wreck or undermine.

clue.text: Perhaps Tarzan wants one to be a passing acquaintance of Simple Simon

indicators.note: wants in the sense of lacks, so a letter is missing

parts.words: a passing acquaintance of Simple Simon
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Simple Simon met a pieman going to the fair
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Tarzan needs someone to be a casual friend of Simple Simon.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'Simple Simon met a pieman, going to the fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, raised in the jungle by apes, is a classic example of a man of the wild.

clue.text: Bucks Fizz destroyed Maoism

indicators.note: a destroyed word is broken up, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A pop group or cocktail ruins Mao's doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks Fizz, champagne and orange juice, is also a British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucks Fizz is the British name for the champagne and orange cocktail called a mimosa in the US.

clue.text: Grub bird picked up after dropping pie

indicators.note: the bird name has had a piece dropped from it

parts.note: the magpie is a black and white bird
taken as written
got means picked up or collected

explanation.surface: A bird took a grub after letting the pie fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the soft larva of a fly, a grub.

clue.text: Decorating drunk — so often spilled gin

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled
spilled liquid splashes everywhere, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Drunk once again, someone hangs decorations, slopping gin around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives FESTOON from SO OFTEN and 'spilled' gives ING from GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Festooning is hanging garlands or chains as ornaments.

clue.text: Politician follows back-up question

indicators.note: follows puts the politician after the reversed piece
back is read as backwards, so the word up is turned round

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP trails behind with a supplementary question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' looks like one word for support, but splits into a reversal signal and its fodder; 'question' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information.

clue.text: Crap, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading either forwards or backwards gives the same word

parts.note: crap is coarse slang for excrement

explanation.surface: Rubbish, from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are coarse slang for excrement or for anything worthless.

clue.text: Song — it could be used to promote a dance?

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

parts.words: it could be used to promote
parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is used for promotion

explanation.surface: A song that might advertise a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BALL AD, an advertisement promoting a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative or sentimental song.

clue.text: Bums without our Scottish bog paper

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the others

parts.note: to bum around is to loll about lazily
oor is the Scots form of our

explanation.surface: Backsides without our Scottish lavatory paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bums' is a verb, lazes about; 'bog' is British slang for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo rolls are rolls of toilet tissue; loo and bog are both British slang for the lavatory.
